claims.text: The untreated refractory high-entropy alloy has a largely single-phase, high-strength microstructure.
The untreated alloy has limited ductility.
The untreated alloy exhibits non-uniform plastic deformation under load.
Adding less than 2 at.% of a ductile alloying element and applying a tailored annealing treatment will form nanoscale ductile precipitates.
The nanoscale precipitates will be evenly distributed and preferentially located at grain boundaries.
The grain-boundary precipitates will provide sites for dislocation accommodation.
The precipitates will reduce local stress concentrations.
The precipitates will facilitate dislocation motion.
Reduced stress concentrations and facilitated dislocation motion will improve ductility and distribute plastic strain more uniformly.
The limited precipitate volume fraction and controlled distribution will allow the matrix to retain its high-strength characteristics.
The limited precipitate volume fraction and controlled distribution will preserve impact-induced energy release.
Relative to the untreated baseline, the treatment is expected to increase strain to failure by approximately 20–30%.
Relative to the untreated baseline, the treatment is expected to produce more uniform plastic deformation.
The treatment is expected to maintain yield strength within a 5–10% variation from the untreated baseline.
The treatment is expected to preserve high impact-induced energy release.
The beneficial effects will occur only within a narrow microalloying and annealing processing window.
Departures from the proposed microalloying concentration or annealing window may cause precipitate coarsening or an excessive secondary-phase fraction.
Precipitate coarsening or an excessive secondary-phase fraction may eliminate the ductility improvement and degrade strength or energetic performance.
